Q1: From round `REVIEW_CONVERGENCE_FROM_ROUND` on, which floor tags keep a finding raised by one reviewer blocking?
Choices:
A. Any floor tag, as the issue says. This includes `FLOOR_HIGH_CONFIDENCE`, which comes from the lone reviewer's own confidence rating, and every `FLOOR_CRITICAL_KEYWORD:*` category (SECURITY, AUTH, CONCURRENCY, RESOURCE, DATA_LOSS, MONGO, NAMING). Many lone findings will still start rounds.
B. Only `FLOOR_CRITICAL_KEYWORD:*` tags, in all categories. A lone finding whose only tag is `FLOOR_HIGH_CONFIDENCE` becomes advisory. `FLOOR_MULTI_REVIEWER` does not count, because the reviewer count comes from the per-reviewer files. (RECOMMENDED)
C. Only `FLOOR_CRITICAL_KEYWORD:SECURITY`, `:AUTH`, `:CONCURRENCY` and `:DATA_LOSS`. RESOURCE, MONGO and NAMING keyword hits and `FLOOR_HIGH_CONFIDENCE` alone become advisory.
Q2: What counts as a "security finding", which always blocks?
Choices:
A. A finding whose consolidator `LENS` is `SECURITY & INPUT VALIDATION` (lens 1) or `IMPLICIT-EXECUTION & TRUST-BOUNDARY RISKS` (lens 9), or one that carries a `FLOOR_CRITICAL_KEYWORD:SECURITY` or `:AUTH` tag. (RECOMMENDED)
B. Only a finding whose `LENS` is `SECURITY & INPUT VALIDATION` (lens 1), or one that carries a `FLOOR_CRITICAL_KEYWORD:SECURITY` or `:AUTH` tag.
C. Only a finding whose `LENS` is `SECURITY & INPUT VALIDATION` (lens 1). The lens label set by the model is the only signal.
**Note:** the SECURITY and AUTH keyword tags already block under every Q1 choice, so the B and C choices here make no difference to them. Q2 only changes how findings without those tags are treated.
